objective: Define the first execution boundary after the accepted non-executing direct command-path native-invocation fixture, while keeping this gate definition-only and avoiding native option support, direct Verilator command execution, sidecar execution, compare execution, timing, speedup, arbitrary filelist support, automatic allocation, runtime/ABI change, raw full-state equality, or production LLM-serving throughput claims.

definition_decision.weakest_point: The phrase native invocation execution boundary can be over-read as proof that a native Verilator command has executed. The accepted fixture only validates metadata: a Verilator-facing argv, parser payload fields, preserved ordinary build inputs, and explicit sidecar context. A later run gate must prove that a built or reviewed Verilator process parsed the accelerator options and then executed only a reviewed sidecar stage authority before any execution, compare, timing, or speedup claim is allowed.
reason: the previous review accepted only metadata validation for a Verilator-facing argv plus explicit sidecar context
the fixture output names the minimum native-looking invocation form but keeps all authority and execution flags false
a future run gate now needs a narrow boundary that separates real process parse evidence from fixture metadata
coverage_output_equivalence remains future compare evidence, not proof from this definition gate
